transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I just haven’t been doing much. I used to go to choir, quilting, visit folks some, but I don’t seem to have the push for it now. Mostly I sit at home with the TV on low, even when I know people are expecting me.
Do you still enjoy the things you used to, like choir or quilting, when you actually do them?
Not much, no. Even if I get myself there, I just… don’t feel much push for choir or quilting like I used to. Mostly I end up staying home, TV on quiet, and let things pass.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say depressed exactly. Just kind of flat, maybe. Hard to say.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest and lack of push?
I guess it’s been coming on since I retired from the school office… a little over two years now.
Do you feel this started because of retiring from your job?
Maybe. I’m not sure it was because of it exactly… but it’s been building since I left the school office, a little over two years ago.
During this time, was there ever a period when you felt clearly depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I don’t think so… not clearly like that. I’ve had low days, but I can’t say it was most of the day every day for two weeks.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical illness that started around the time these changes began?
Not that I can think of… nothing new that started around then, no.
Have these changes made it hard for you to manage your usual responsibilities or relationships?

Yes… some. I don’t keep up like I used to. I stepped back from leading choir and from helping with things at the senior center, because I’d say I’d do something and then… not manage it. And my church friends check on me more now.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?
I don’t know… I worry some, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say a lot. Not all the time.
Do you find yourself still dwelling a lot on having retired?
Not really… I mean, I think about it sometimes, but I don’t sit around dwelling on it a lot.
Have you felt down or sad more days than not over the past two years?
I don’t think so… I have my low days, but I wouldn’t say it’s been more days than not for that long.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory?
Not really… I mean, I forget little things sometimes, but nothing that seems like a real problem.
During this time, have you often felt sad or empty?
Not often, no… I mean, I get quiet sometimes, but I wouldn’t say sad or empty a lot.
Have you noticed a change in your sleep?
I don’t think there’s been much change… I sleep about the same, far as I can tell.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite?
Not that I’ve noticed… I eat about the same, I guess.
Have you been feeling tired or low on energy?
Not really… I mean, I get tired like anybody, but I haven’t noticed it being more than usual.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I don’t know… not really. I haven’t noticed much trouble with that.
Have you had any neurological illness, like a stroke or Parkinson’s disease?
No… not that I know of. I haven’t had anything like that.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
Hopeless? … No, I don’t think so. Not really.
Do you still get pleasure from anything?
A little, maybe… but not like before. I used to like choir and quilting, visiting people. Now I mostly just sit home with the TV on low. I know folks expect me, but I just don’t have the push.
